1. One could probably blame Fortuona for Mat's initial plan, but - despite my more or less blind spot for the Seanchan - I have to agree with the previous speaker who said that it had more to do with flushing out the Shadow's influence before going for a head-on assault. 

2. Rand is now something... else. The same soul in a new body, free to live and die like a mortal man, just like he thinks himself in the epilogue. I'm confident this seemingly magic ability, having nothing to do with neither One nor True Power, is something tied to his thread in the Pattern. Maybe this is an ability connected to every Dragon of every Age that succeeded in his quest? To be free of both others and the responsibility connected to him, cleverly hidden underneath a new face. Absolute freedom. I cannot but envy him.

3. I'm confident that this is Nakomi. Her appearance more or less out of nowhere and what she says almost certainly proves the theory of her divine origin true; that she is either an agent of the Creator or even something like the Creator himself in a very careful disguise. 

4. Well, Osan'gar had had his chance(s) and I guess the Dark One was extremely disappointed. Sammael was probably not resurrected because the Dark One expected more of him. That's my opinion, any way.

5. The Broken Wolf is Perrin, as stated by Brandon Sanderson. The substitute for his name is mentioned in the ''Towers of Midnight'' prologue in the ''Prophecies of the Shadow''. This is most likely the reason it never came true; since the Light's prophecies did come true, the Shadow's could not.

6. I'm sure Hawkwing wouldn't mind having his great-great-great-and-so-on-son-in-law as a Hero of the Horn. But as Hend the Striker assured Mat, he is no Hero, and neither does Mat want to be one.

7. As a previous speaker stated, they are no longer vital for the storyline. Dobraine is no Steward of the Dragon, and Sulin has not been at Rand's side since ''A Crown of Swords'', I believe.
